escalations.hypothesis: The decomposer split one coupled interface, the agentType name string, across two parallel tasks and gave neither a contract for it. The spec never names the new types. t1 (definitions) named them after call-site labels (spec.md, route.md, decompose.md, tiebreak.md, integrate-resolve.md, ...). t2 (bindings) had to bind each workflow site to a type that did not exist in its worktree, so it invented role names (spec-writer.md, risk-router.md, decomposer.md, tiebreak-judge.md, integrator.md, ...) and wrote those 12 definitions itself so its bindings would resolve. The two patches (.artifacts/diffs/t1-agent-definitions.r0.patch, t2-workflow-bindings.r0.patch) now disagree on every name, and neither patch works without the other. Recommended fix is kill_to_spec: add the 12 agentType names to the spec (or merge t1 and t2 into one task that owns both .claude/agents/ and the workflow files), then re-decompose. guide would only work if the human names the canonical names in args and tells t2 to delete its 12 .md files and rebind to t1's names.

escalations.hypothesis: The task is stuck on a test bug, and the implementation looks fine. The Test Author's helper resolves REPO from its own location under .artifacts/tests/, which points at the main checkout (16 baseline agent definitions). The implementer's 12 new definitions sit in .artifacts/worktrees/t1-agent-definitions (28 files), so the test cannot pass however the implementation is fixed. Round 1 then spent 2x the per-round budget with nothing it could fix. Suggested fix: make the test root injectable (for example, an env var such as AGENT_DEFS_REPO defaulting to the cwd, with tests run from inside the worktree), or copy the test into the worktree before running it. Then re-run verification on the existing implementation, since nothing in it needs to change.
